issue_context.title: Control flow migration fails for async pipe with unboxing of observable.
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

I run the control flow migration on my code and it failed compilation.

before:
<ng-container *ngIf="value$ | async; let value">
	{{value}}
</ng-container>

after:
@if (value$ | async; let value) {
{{value}}
}

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

_No response_

review_comments: If you want to add tests for the other scenarios (If/else, If/then/else, and NgIfElse) that would be great, but non-blocking. I think this covers the logic well enough.
I add the missing test cases.
Can you add this to the other 3 cases also? Lines 109, 116, and 154 would also need this fix.

Hi @jessicajaniuk, thank you for your review.

Regarding line 109 for bound if else blocks, I don’t believe my fix is applicable. In this case, I think we should use a template input variable with let- as follows:
[ngIf]="logStatus$ | async" let-logStatus

@AnthonyFr75 I think it would apply to 109, but yeah, not 116. 109 applies to regular usages of if/else: `*ngIf="condition; else tmpl"`. 116 is for the bound usages of it that would have `[ngIf]` and `[ngIfElse]`.

Hi @jessicajaniuk, I just noticed that it would not apply to standard 'if-else-then' structures, either. In the code snippet: `
Not displayed on the DOM, so logStatus is not be available
Hello Bye bye ` The logStatus input variable cannot be accessed by the templates. Additionally, the text inside the div is not displayed in the DOM because its rendering has been delegated to the templates.
@AnthonyFr75 Thanks for checking and verifying that!
